Assume Countable Choice. Let $E$ be a smooth real rank-$2m$ vector bundle on $S=\mathbb R_s\times[0,1]_t$, $m\ge1$, with a smooth endomorphism $J$ satisfying $J^2=-I$. On the two boundary edges let $F_0,F_1$ be smooth real rank-$m$ subbundles with $F_j\cap JF_j=0$. Suppose that outside a compact strip there are specified smooth complex frames $\tau_\pm:\mathbb C^m\to E$, intertwining $i$ and $J$, in which $F_0=\mathbb R^m$ and $F_1=i\mathbb R^m$. Let $P$ be a smooth real linear first-order operator on sections of $E$ with symbol
$$P(f\xi)=fP\xi+f_s\xi+f_tJ\xi$$
for every smooth real function $f$, and suppose its expression in each end frame is exactly $\partial_s+i\partial_t$ outside a compact strip.

There exist a global smooth complex frame $\Phi$, a sign matrix $S_+=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma,1,\ldots,1)$ with $\sigma\in\{1,-1\}$, an integer $\ell$, and a smooth real function $\vartheta(s)$, constant at $\pi/2$ on the negative end and $\pi/2+\ell\pi$ on the positive end, such that $\Phi=\tau_-$ on the negative end, $\Phi=\tau_+S_+$ on the positive end, and
$$F_0=\Phi\mathbb R^m,\qquad F_1=\Phi\left(e^{i\vartheta(s)}\mathbb R\times i\mathbb R^{m-1}\right).$$
In this frame $P$ is $\partial_s+i\partial_t+B(s,t)$ with smooth compactly supported real linear $B$. On the $H^1$ completion of compactly supported smooth sections satisfying those actual boundary subbundles, with the norm defined by finite bundle charts on a compact core and the prescribed frames on the ends, $P$ maps to the corresponding $L^2(E)$ space and is real Fredholm, with
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}P=-\ell.$$
The same index holds with the weight $e^{\delta|s|}$ for $0\le\delta<\pi/2$. These are indices before any translation quotient. The integer $\ell$ is independent of the choices in the construction, since it is minus the index of this fixed operator.

In particular the conclusion applies to the actual linearization at a smooth $J_t$-holomorphic strip of finite Dirichlet energy, measured in a smooth target metric, in a compact target, with compact totally real boundary submanifolds of transverse finite intersection, whenever the chosen target charts at their intersections identify those submanifolds with $\mathbb R^m,i\mathbb R^m$ and $J_t$ with the constant structure $i$ for every $t$. For product Heegaard tori such a geometric choice is available by the product-integrable generator-neighborhood construction. No domain Euler-measure formula, corner/excision theorem, generic regularity, or moduli count is part of this conclusion.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $S=\mathbb R_s\times[0,1]_t$, $m\ge1$, and $0<\theta_j<\pi$. Write $X_0=H^1_\theta$ for the real $H^1$ completion of smooth maps compactly supported in $s$ satisfying $u(s,0)\in\mathbb R^m$ and $u(s,1)\in\prod_j e^{i\theta_j}\mathbb R$. Let $B:S\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb R}(\mathbb C^m)$ be smooth up to the boundary, with every derivative bounded, and suppose its uniform end limits are real diagonal matrices $\operatorname{diag}(b_{\pm,j})$ with $\theta_j-b_{\pm,j}\notin\pi\mathbb Z$. For an integer $q\ge0$ put
$$X_q=H^{q+1}(S;\mathbb C^m)\cap X_0,\qquad Y_q=H^q(S;\mathbb C^m),\qquad T_q=\partial_s+i\partial_t+B:X_q\longrightarrow Y_q,$$
using real Hilbert spaces and their indicated Sobolev norms. There are no higher boundary conditions: only the zeroth trace encoded by $X_0$ is required. In particular no normal derivative or forcing trace is prescribed.

Every $T_q$ is bounded Fredholm. Its kernel is the same set as the kernel of $T_0$, and its range is $Y_q\cap\operatorname{Ran}T_0$. The inclusion of $Y_q$ in $L^2$ induces an isomorphism of real cokernels. Thus
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}T_q=\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}T_0=\sum_j\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\theta_j-b_{-,j}}\pi\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\frac{\theta_j-b_{+,j}}\pi\right\rfloor\right).$$
More precisely, if $u\in X_0$ and $T_0u=f\in H^q$, then $u\in X_q$ and
$$\|u\|_{H^{q+1}}\le C_q\bigl(\|f\|_{H^q}+\|u\|_{H^1}\bigr).$$

The same conclusions hold with smooth two-sided weights $w=e^{\delta\rho(s)}$, where $\rho$ is smooth, equals $|s|$ outside a compact interval, has all derivatives of positive order bounded, and $0\le\delta<\min_{\pm,j,n}|\pi n-\theta_j+b_{\pm,j}|$. Weighted spaces mean $wu\in X_q$ and $wf\in Y_q$. Their index is the same displayed index. The weight is smooth at zero even for $q\ge1$.

Finally, for an actual geometric strip operator with exact product-integrable ends and the smooth bundle frame supplied by the geometric strip normal-form theorem, the actual $H^{q+1}$ boundary-section domain and $H^q$ target have this same real index before translation quotient, also with these smooth weights. This asserts integer Hilbert Sobolev agreement; no $W^{1,p}$ comparison or Heegaard-domain Euler formula is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary, and let $J(s,t,x)$ be a smooth family of almost complex structures on $X$, defined for $(s,t)$ in an open subset $U\subset\mathbb R^2$. Suppose the norms of $J$ and its derivatives through total order two, using the Levi-Civita connection in $X$ and ordinary derivatives in $s,t$, are uniformly bounded. Then there are constants $a,b\ge0$, depending only on these bounds and $g$, such that every smooth solution
$$u_s+J(s,t,u)u_t=0$$
has energy density $e=(|u_s|_g^2+|u_t|_g^2)/2$ satisfying
$$\Delta e\ge-ae^2-be.$$
Consequently there are $r_0,\varepsilon_0>0$ depending only on the same data such that, whenever $\overline B_r(z)\subset U$, $0<r\le r_0$, and $\int_{B_r(z)}e<\varepsilon_0$, one has
$$|du(z)|_g^2\le\frac{32}{3\pi r^2}\int_{B_r(z)}e.$$
These are interior estimates for smooth actual solutions. No boundary estimate or higher-derivative compactness is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X$ be a compact smooth manifold without boundary, with a background Riemannian metric $g_0$, and let $L\subset X$ be a compact embedded submanifold without boundary of half its real dimension. Let $J(s,t,x)$ be a smooth uniformly $C^2$ bounded family of almost complex structures for parameters in a neighborhood of a closed upper half-disk. Suppose $J(s,0,x)=J_b(x)$ for $x\in L$, independently of $s$, where $TL\cap J_bTL=0$.

There is a smooth Riemannian metric $g$ on $X$, depending only on $g_0,L,J_b$, such that $J_b$ is orthogonal and $J_bTL$ is perpendicular to $TL$ along $L$. For this metric there are constants $r_0,\varepsilon_0>0$ depending only on the geometric data and uniform family bounds with the following property. If $0<r\le r_0$ and a smooth map $u:\overline B_r^+\to X$ solves $u_s+J(s,t,u)u_t=0$, maps the flat edge into $L$, and satisfies $E=\int_{B_r^+}e_g<\varepsilon_0$, then
$$|du(0,0)|_g^2\le\frac{32}{\pi r^2}E,\qquad \sup_{B_{r/2}^+}|du|_g^2\le\frac{128}{\pi r^2}E,$$
where $e_g=(|u_s|_g^2+|u_t|_g^2)/2$. Uniformly equivalent estimates with constants depending on the data hold for $g_0$. No assumption that the whole image lies in one coordinate chart is made.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $S=\mathbb R\times[0,1]$, let $(X,g_0)$ be compact without boundary, and let $L_0,L_1\subset X$ be compact embedded submanifolds without boundary, of half the real dimension of $X$. Suppose smooth almost complex families $J_n(s,t,x)$ have uniform bounds for all derivatives on $S\times X$, converge in $C^\infty$ on compact subsets to $J_\infty$, and satisfy $J_n(s,j,x)=J_{b,j}(x)$ for $x\in L_j$, $j=0,1$, independently of $n,s$. Suppose $TL_j\cap J_{b,j}TL_j=0$.

Let $u_n:S\to X$ be smooth up to the boundary, with $u_n(s,j)\in L_j$, satisfying $(u_n)_s+J_n(s,t,u_n)(u_n)_t=0$, and with $g_0$-energies at most $E_0<\infty$. There is a constant $\varepsilon>0$ depending only on the geometric data and uniform coefficient bounds, a finite set $Z\subset S$ with $|Z|\le\lfloor E_0/\varepsilon\rfloor$, and a subsequence converging in $C^\infty$ on every compact subset of $S\setminus Z$, including one-sided derivatives at its boundary, to a map $u_\infty$. The limit satisfies the $J_\infty$ equation, the indicated boundary conditions, and has energy at most $E_0$ on $S\setminus Z$.

This assertion does not extend the map across $Z$, recover lost energy, construct bubble trees, or describe strip breaking at either noncompact end.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,g)$ be compact and $L\subset X$ a fixed compact totally real submanifold. On the closed upper half-disk let smooth almost complex families $J_n(z,x)$ converge smoothly locally to $J_\infty$, with uniform coefficient bounds, and suppose $J_n(s,x)=J_b(x)$ for real $s$ and $x\in L$, independent of $n,s$. Let smooth solutions $u_n:B_1^+\to X$, smooth up to the straight boundary with values there on $L$, have uniformly bounded energy and converge smoothly locally off $0$, including boundary points, to a solution $u$ smoothly filled at $0$. Suppose concentric half-disk energies have limits with positive atom mass $m$ at $0$.

There is a uniform $h>0$ such that $m\ge h$ and, after a subsequence, real centers $a_n\to0$, positive scales $\rho_n\to0$, an autonomous $J_\infty(0,x)$-holomorphic disk $v$ with boundary on $L$, and finitely many child atoms $Z\subset\overline{\mathbb H}$ have these properties. The rescaled maps $v_n(w)=u_n(a_n+\rho_nw)$ converge smoothly locally off $Z$ to $v$, on the upper half-plane including its straight boundary. Moreover
$$\lim_{R\to\infty}\lim_nE_g(v_n;B_R^+)=m=E_g(v)+\sum_{z\in Z}m_z,\qquad v(\infty)=u(0).$$
Every child has mass at least $h$. Boundary children satisfy $m_z\le m-h$; interior children satisfy $m_z\le m$. If $v$ is constant then
$$|Z\cap\mathbb R|+2|Z\cap\mathbb H|\ge2.$$
Thus the constant disk is stable after including its parent boundary node at infinity. The connecting half-annuli have vanishing energy and image diameter. The same $h$ works for descendants. These conclusions constitute one actual boundary soft-rescaling step.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix compact target and coefficient bounds as in the interior and boundary cylinder-neck lemmas. Let $D$ be either an angular circle of fixed length $T$, or the interval $[0,T]$ with both edges on the same fixed compact totally real $L$ and with fixed boundary structure $J_b$. Coefficient bounds include uniform $C^2$ bounds in source and target, and, in the boundary case, $J(\sigma,0,x)=J(\sigma,T,x)=J_b(x)$ for $x\in L$.

There are constants $\delta_0,\kappa_0,c,C>0$ depending only on these data such that the following holds. Let $u$ be a smooth actual almost complex solution on $[a-1,b+1]\times D$, with explicit source derivatives of $J$ bounded by $\kappa_0$. Suppose $0<\delta\le\delta_0$ and every source disk or physical-boundary half-disk of one fixed radius $r_0<\min\{1/8,T/16\}$, contained in this cylinder, has energy at most $\delta$. Then for $0\le R\le(b-a)/2$,
$$E_g(u;[a+R,b-R]\times D)\le C\delta e^{-cR},$$
and
$$\operatorname{diam}_g u([a+R,b-R]\times D)\le C\sqrt\delta e^{-cR/2}.$$
In particular, for any sequence of such necks, their central energy and image diameter tend uniformly to zero as their distance $R$ from the ends tends to infinity. This is a criterion for a neck already satisfying the stated local-energy bound; no bubble-tree decomposition is assumed or asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix compact $(X,g)$, compact transverse totally real boundary submanifolds $L_0,L_1$ with finite intersection $K$, and smooth families $J_{n,t}$ converging smoothly to $J_{\infty,t}$. Their boundary structures on $L_0,L_1$ are fixed independently of $n$. Assume all these structures are exactly $i$ on common disjoint product generator charts taking $L_0,L_1$ to transverse product real lines, as in the actual transverse-strip neck lemma. Let smooth finite-energy solutions
$$\partial_su_n+J_{n,t}(u_n)\partial_tu_n=0,\qquad u_n(s,j)\in L_j,$$
on $\mathbb R\times[0,1]$ have energies at most $E_0$.

After a subsequence, either all maps are one constant generator, or there are finitely many longitudinal translations $q_{1,n}<\cdots<q_{M,n}$ with $q_{j+1,n}-q_{j,n}\to\infty$ and finitely many bubbled strip levels. Each level consists of a finite-energy $J_{\infty,t}$ strip, possibly constant, with finite sphere/disk bubble trees at its interior or physical boundary points. These are the actual local rescaling limits, have equal component values at their nodes, and constant bubbles satisfy the usual sphere node count or weighted disk node count. Each level has positive energy when its bubbles are included. The translated maps converge smoothly locally off the bubble points, including boundary derivatives, and all bubbles are smooth rescaled limits off their children.

After fixing the original end generators by a subsequence, adjacent strip levels have equal intermediate end generators, the first negative end and last positive end are the original ones, and
$$\lim_nE_g(u_n)=\sum_{j=1}^M\left(E_g(v_j)+\sum_{w\text{ on level }j}E_g(u_w)\right).$$
There is no energy or image diameter left between successive level cores or outside the first and last cores as their radii tend to infinity after the sequence limit. The number of levels and bubble components is uniformly bounded in terms of $E_0$ and the fixed geometric data. No exclusion of bubbles, index bound, regularity, or gluing is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,g)$ be compact, with compact totally real boundary submanifolds $L_0,L_1$ having finite transverse intersection $K$. Let $J_t$ be smooth, independent of the longitudinal variable, with fixed boundary structures on $L_0,L_1$. Suppose there are disjoint generator charts about $K$ in which $L_0=\mathbb R^m$, $L_1=\prod_j e^{i\theta_j(x)}\mathbb R$, $0<\theta_j(x)<\pi$, and $J_t=i$ for every $t$. Such actual auxiliary choices exist in the product-torus setting by the generator-neighborhood lemma.

There are constants $\delta_0,c,C>0$ such that the following holds. Let $u$ be a smooth solution on $[a-1,b+1]\times[0,1]$ with these boundary conditions, and suppose every window $[s-1/2,s+1/2]\times[0,1]$, $s\in[a,b]$, has energy at most $\delta\le\delta_0$. Then the image of $[a,b]\times[0,1]$ lies in one of the generator charts. For $1\le R\le(b-a)/2$,
$$E_g(u;[a+R,b-R]\times[0,1])\le C\delta e^{-cR},$$
and its image has diameter at most $C\sqrt\delta e^{-cR/2}$ and lies within that distance of that chart's generator. The constants are independent of neck length. The same bounds hold on a semi-infinite neck, measuring distance from its finite end.

Every actual nonconstant finite-energy strip on $\mathbb R\times[0,1]$ with these fixed data has energy at least $\delta_0$, after possibly decreasing that constant. No regularity, index, or gluing theorem is presupposed.

Assume Countable Choice. Put $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m\Sigma$ for a closed connected Riemann surface, and fix finitely many product tori $L_j$ from systems of pairwise disjoint attaching curves. Let $a\in\Sigma$ lie off all these curves. The actual point-divisor bundle of $E_a=\{a\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}\Sigma$, with its canonical section on the boundary, defines integer degrees $n_a$ for disks and spheres, including contained spheres. It also defines an integer for every smooth strip between two transverse specified tori, with simultaneous product generator charts and uniform ends at their intersections: truncate and cap its ends inside sufficiently small generator charts avoiding $E_a$. The integer is independent of the sufficiently remote cuts and these local caps, and agrees with proper holomorphic intersection multiplicity whenever the latter is defined.

In the actual bounded-energy compactness conclusions of the bordered-source bubble-tree theorem, when the fixed source is a disk, or of the bubbled transverse-strip breaking theorem, these degrees satisfy, for all sufficiently large sequence indices,
$$n_a(u_n)=\sum_{\text{base or strip levels }v}n_a(v)+\sum_{\text{bubble components }w}n_a(w).$$
The hypotheses of those compactness theorems, including their common exact transverse generator charts for strips, are retained. No avoidance of $E_a$ by interior nodes or sphere bubbles is required. The formula holds simultaneously for any fixed finite set of such points.

In particular suppose the strip sequence satisfies that transverse-strip compactness theorem and the compact-bubble domain-energy lemma, with common diagonal and region-divisor neighborhoods and uniformly bounded geometric constants. Let $z_1,\ldots,z_k$ be marked points off all attaching curves, with $J_{n,t}$ and its limit equal to the standard symmetric-product structure near their divisors. Require that each connected component of the complement of each individual boundary curve system contains at least one of these marked points. If $n_{z_i}(u_n)=0$ for every $i,n$, its limit has no nonconstant sphere or disk bubbles. In fact no bubble vertices remain after discarding redundant constant vertices, and every retained strip level is nonconstant and has $n_{z_i}=0$ for every $i$. Thus that actual compactness theorem reduces to finite breaking of unbubbled zero-marked strips, with its smooth local convergence and full energy and neck-collapse conclusions. This does not assert regularity of same-generator index-two strips, a Maslov/domain-index identity, low-index stratum dimensions, or gluing.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,g)$ be compact, let $L_0,L_1\subset X$ be compact smooth half-dimensional submanifolds with finite intersection, and let $J(s,t,x)$ be smooth almost complex structures on $[0,\infty)\times[0,1]\times X$ with uniform $C^2$ bounds in source and target. Assume $J(s,j,x)=J_{b,j}(x)$ for $x\in L_j$, independent of $s$, and that $L_j$ is totally real for $J_{b,j}$. A smooth solution
$$u_s+J(s,t,u)u_t=0,\qquad u(s,j)\in L_j,$$
with finite Dirichlet energy has a unique point $x_+\in L_0\cap L_1$ such that
$$\sup_{0\le t\le1}d_g(u(s,t),x_+)\longrightarrow0,\qquad \sup_{0\le t\le1}|du(s,t)|_g\longrightarrow0$$
as $s\to\infty$. In particular no such strip exists if $L_0\cap L_1$ is empty. Compact transverse half-dimensional $L_0,L_1$ satisfy the finite-intersection premise. The analogous conclusion holds at a negative strip end. No exponential rate or index theorem is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice and the actual finite-energy half-strip hypotheses of [[lem-finite-energy-transverse-strip-end-convergence]]. Suppose additionally that at each point $x\in L_0\cap L_1$ there is a smooth target coordinate chart $q_x$ centered at $x$, taking the two boundary submanifolds locally to
$$\mathbb R^m,\qquad \prod_{j=1}^m e^{i\theta_j(x)}\mathbb R,\qquad 0<\theta_j(x)<\pi,$$
and taking $J(s,t,\cdot)$ to the constant structure $i$ throughout that neighborhood for all source $s,t$. These are concrete geometric choice hypotheses, not moduli-space axioms.

Let $x_+$ be the end limit. On a sufficiently far tail put $v=q_{x_+}\circ u$ and $\gamma_+=\min_j(\pi-\theta_j(x_+))>0$. For every integer $k\ge0$ there is $C_k<\infty$ such that
$$\sup_{0\le t\le1}|D^k v(s,t)|\le C_k e^{-\gamma_+s}.$$
For every $0\le\delta<\gamma_+$ and every finite $k$, the map $e^{\delta s}v$ belongs to $H^k$ on a far tail. Thus all derivatives converge exponentially to the constant generator. Constructing the prescribed coordinate charts and an admissible global $J$ with these values is a separate prerequisite.

Assume countable choice. Retain the compact target, totally real boundary submanifolds, fixed path $J_t$ and exact product generator charts of the smooth relative-homotopy index lemma. A continuous Whitney representative from $x$ to $y$ is a continuous disk map with two specified boundary points mapped to $x,y$ and its two boundary arcs mapped into $L_0,L_1$. Equivalence means an actual continuous relative homotopy fixing those points and preserving the two boundary conditions.

Every such class has a smooth fixed-end strip representative, constant on full tails. If two smooth fixed-end representatives are continuously relatively homotopic, there is a smooth relative homotopy between them with one common pair of constant tails and the same fixed endpoints. Consequently the quotient of smooth fixed-end representatives by those smooth homotopies identifies with the continuous Whitney-class set. The actual real Fredholm index of its fixed-end Cauchy–Riemann-symbol linearization therefore defines an integer $\mu(\phi)$ on every continuous Whitney class; it agrees with the actual index of each smooth fixed-end model, is additive under class concatenation, is zero on the constant class, and changes sign under reversal.

For an actual smooth finite-energy holomorphic strip with uniform generator ends, its actual Fredholm index equals this index of its continuously compactified Whitney class.

This proves a continuous-class index using genuine representatives and relative homotopies. It does not identify that integer with a domain Euler measure, corner multiplicities or a first-Chern pairing; no nonlinear moduli counts or their regularity are asserted.

Assume countable choice. Let $X$ be a compact smooth manifold with a smooth path $J_t$ of almost complex structures, and let $L_0,L_1$ be compact submanifolds totally real for $J_0,J_1$, respectively. Suppose their intersection is finite and transverse. At each intersection point choose a target chart in which $L_0=\mathbb R^m$, $L_1=i\mathbb R^m$ and $J_t=i$ for every $t$. Retain those same charts and structures throughout.

A smooth fixed-end representative from $x$ to $y$ is a smooth map $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to X$ with boundary on $L_0,L_1$, identically $x$ on one full negative tail and identically $y$ on one full positive tail. Its covariant Cauchy–Riemann linearization on fixed-end $H^1\to L^2$ spaces is Fredholm. Its real index is independent of the chosen smooth connection and of the representative under any smooth relative homotopy $H(h,s,t)$ with those boundary conditions, fixed endpoints, and one common pair of constant tails for all $h\in[0,1]$.

These indices add under concatenating two such representatives at their common endpoint, are zero for a constant representative, and change sign when $u(s,t)$ is replaced by $u(-s,t)$. Thus they define an integer index on smooth fixed-end representatives modulo the stated smooth relative homotopies, with concatenation and reversal laws. This result includes nonholomorphic representatives. It does not assume that a nonlinear moduli space exists or is regular.

A further relative smoothing and end-flattening argument is required to identify this smooth quotient with a Whitney-class set defined initially by arbitrary continuous disk maps and continuous relative homotopies. No such identification, domain Euler formula, or arbitrary-class representativity theorem is asserted here.

Assume Countable Choice. In the compact transverse geometry with common exact product generator charts, let an actual sequence of strips have the unbubbled breaking conclusion of the strip compactness theorem, with nonconstant levels $v_1,\ldots,v_M$, matched end generators and no additional energy or image diameter on the intermediate necks or outer tails. Each strip determines its continuous Whitney class by filling its two uniform generator ends, with boundary arcs on $L_0,L_1$. Concatenation joins matching constant end neighborhoods, or equivalently the corresponding marked disk ends.

For all sufficiently large $n$, the actual relative classes satisfy
$$[u_n]=[v_1]*\cdots*[v_M].$$
These are classes under continuous homotopies fixing the two marked ends and preserving each boundary arc. The conclusion uses the actual image collapse and smooth core convergence, not just equality of divisor degrees or energy. It applies in particular to the actual zero-marked unbubbled compactness conclusion, without any additional index hypothesis.

For the actual regular-pair pregluing $u_R$ and Newton-corrected strip $g_R$ in the regular-strip gluing lemma, for all sufficiently large $R$ one has
$$[g_R]=[u_R]=[u^-]*[u^+].$$
No converse classification of relative classes, Maslov/domain formula, or gluing for bubbles or degenerating targets is asserted.

derivations.claim:
In genus zero the target is a point: every map is constant, its section spaces are zero, and the entire assertion follows with no end levels and index zero. Assume positive genus for the remaining proof. The actual central linearization has formula $P_u\xi=
abla_s\xi+J(s,t,u)
abla_t\xi+(
abla_\xi J)(s,t,u)u_t$; differentiating the map variable introduces no derivative of the prescribed source arguments. Its real principal symbol is exactly the Cauchy--Riemann symbol. Uniform generator ends put each far tail inside its exact product chart, where the equation and its coordinate linearization are exactly $D_0=\partial_s+i\partial_t$, with real and imaginary boundary planes. The transverse end expansion in [F5] applies there. The bundle-symbol assertion of [F1] therefore gives the actual Fredholm operator and higher range agreement. To identify its index, first flatten the exponential tails to their generators by scalar cutoffs inside those product charts. The index is unchanged: the completed squared boundary phase loop is homotoped only inside the same fixed end chart, where the two added cap phases cancel. Interpolate the prescribed $J(s,t)$ to the fixed background using its small Cayley coefficients; all generator charts and boundary end values stay fixed. A joint complex frame on the compact nonconstant core is constructed by the finite projection ODE in [F1]. The completed boundary phase consequently varies by a genuine loop homotopy. Its winding, hence actual index, is constant. The flattened map now has exactly the smooth relative index in [F5], so the central index is the geometric Whitney index, including for nonautonomous solutions. This proves the claimed operator assertion without importing an autonomous-solution hypothesis. [F1, F5, given, construct, algebra]

Apply [F2]'s local energy estimates and Sobolev bootstrap on each compact rectangle. Countable diagonal extraction gives smooth convergence off finitely many energy concentrations on each such rectangle, and finite total energy bounds their total number by $E_0/h$, with the positive local bubble quantum $h$. At an interior concentration use the actual interior soft-rescaling induction; at a physical edge use its boundary version. Those are local disk/half-disk arguments. They do not impose an artificial totally real condition on the curved boundary of a chosen local half-disk or on a rectangle's vertical cuts. This gives the actual finite bubble trees, their full energy identities and connecting collapsed necks at every finite concentration. The remaining anchored map solves the limiting source-dependent equation smoothly after the actual puncture-removal step in those proofs. Its energy is finite. The small-window estimate needed here and below does not require an autonomous source. Indeed [F2]'s actual source-dependent epsilon estimates bound $|du|$ by $C\sqrt\delta$ on every buffered window of energy $\delta$. Every angular slice then has small length. Compactness of the two boundaries and their finite transverse intersection force its two endpoints into one of the finitely many separated generator neighborhoods; the entire short slice remains in that chart. Connectedness forces a whole connected small-window neck into one chart. There the equation is EXACTLY $D_0v=0$, since all prescribed source-dependent structures agree with $i$ on that chart. The actual Fourier proof in [F3] then gives the same energy and diameter decay, with uniform constants. For the finite-energy central map all sufficiently far windows have arbitrarily small energy, so each whole tail lies in one chart. Slice Poincare and the positive spectral gap give its generator limit and all-order exponential expansion by [F5]. This proves the central end assertion without an autonomous-source end theorem being applied outside its hypotheses. It may be constant, and that possibility is retained as the anchored central component. No translation of this compact source core has been made. [F2, F3, F5, given, construct, algebra]

Account for every component escaping to longitudinal infinity. Fix the bad-window threshold $\delta>0$ from [F3] and retain the source interval $[-10,10]$ as an anchor. The continuous function $A_n(s)=E(u_n;[s-2,s+2]\times[0,1])$ tends to zero on both infinite tails, so $B_n=\{s:A_n(s)\ge\delta\}$ is compact. If it is nonempty, select its least point, then the least remaining point at least four to its right, and continue. The corresponding windows have disjoint interiors, so there are at most $\lfloor E_0/\delta\rfloor$ selections. Every point of $B_n$ lies between a selected point and four units to its right, since otherwise it would be an available next selection. Include the anchor at zero in the finite cluster list, whether or not it is bad. After subsequences their bounded-offset clusters either remain at a bounded distance from the anchor or escape to one of the two infinities. Bounded clusters are already part of step 1.2. Each escaping cluster, translated to its center, has on every fixed source rectangle coefficients converging with every derivative to $J^-_\infty$ or $J^+_\infty$, by the uniform tail hypothesis. Thus [F3]'s same local extraction, rescaling and end argument gives a finite-energy strip level there with its possible local bubble trees; before bubble exclusion that strip may be constant if a bubble carries the cluster energy. Different clusters have distances tending to infinity. Between clusters, beyond the outermost clusters and between the anchor and its nearest clusters every fixed-size window is below the common threshold. The actual source-dependent small-window argument proved in step 1.2 puts every buffered long gap inside one exact generator chart and makes its central energy and diameter tend to zero. The finite energy identity inside the retained cores then captures ALL energy; there is no residual escaping component or neck energy. The matching generator limits agree because each connecting image diameter tends to zero. The escaping limit levels themselves are autonomous by coefficient convergence. The finite-window extraction and source-dependent neck argument do not require exact autonomy of each approximating map, and keep the central core anchored. [F2, F3, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

Now eliminate all the bubble trees, rather than assuming their absence in the extraction. Use [F4]'s connection for the fixed divisor $E_z$. It is independent of the source and is flat near the tori and generator charts. Integrals over the smooth component cores converge. The absolute integral over any omitted neck or energy tail is bounded by its energy times one common curvature bound, and tends to zero by steps 1.2 and 2.1. The frame-Stokes formula in [F4] therefore expresses the integer $n_z(u_n)=0$ as the sum of the degrees of the central strip, every end level and every actual compact sphere or disk bubble. This argument uses a fixed TARGET line bundle and no autonomous-source or squared-determinant index connection. Every term is nonnegative by protected-divisor positivity for strips and by the compact bubble positivity in [F4]. Hence each compact bubble has zero mark degree. For a sphere its domain is $d\Sigma$; for a one-torus disk its domain is constant on each cut component. The chosen $z$ meets the sole cut component of either complete system. [F4] then makes every such zero-mark bubble constant. The local stability rules remove all remaining ghost-only trees: a finite tree of constant bubbles with no active component has a terminal component with too few distinguished points, contrary to the explicitly stabilized extraction. Thus there are no bubble trees. Each escaping cluster retains at least $\delta$ energy on a sufficiently large fixed translated core by its bad center and local energy identity; with bubbles excluded its strip level is therefore nonconstant. Only the anchored central component may remain constant. Steps 1.2 and 2.1 now give exactly the smooth central and end components, energy identity and matched necks in the Statement. [F4, step 1.2, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

Fix sufficiently far generator cuts on each of the finitely many limiting components. They and all the connecting necks lie in the same exact product charts for large $n$, by step 3.1. Multiply the coordinate maps on successive necks by real scalar cutoffs, retaining their two physical boundary planes and contracting their middle portions to the common generator. This is an actual continuous relative homotopy, with the outer ends fixed. On every retained finite core the sequence is uniformly close to its limit. The boundary-preserving local-addition straight homotopy identifies these cores with the limiting ones; the remaining finite cutoff tails are homotoped inside their product charts. This is precisely the topological construction in [F5]'s actual class-splitting proof, which uses only core convergence, physical boundary preservation and collapsed generator necks, not autonomy of the central equation. Consequently $[u_n]$ is eventually the ordered concatenation of the end classes with the anchored central class. Apply the additive continuous Whitney index from [F5] and the actual source-dependent operator identification in step 1.1. This gives the asserted equality of actual indices. A constant central component has the constant transverse $D_0$ operator and index zero, so retaining it contributes no false translation parameter or index shift. [F1, F5, step 1.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra] ∎

citations.quote:
Assume Countable Choice. Give an actual complete singly pointed Heegaard diagram of ANY closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold $Y$, with transverse attaching systems, one-ball compression cuts, basepoint $z$, a reference orientation-compatible Riemann surface structure and a positive area form. Suppose it is GLOBALLY weakly admissible: every nonzero periodic region domain with $n_z=0$ has both signs. Broad smooth tangencies of auxiliary compression-disk witnesses are permitted.

There is a choice of surface complex structure, protected region and marked-divisor neighborhoods, common product-integrable generator charts and a nearly symmetric tame path constant on genuine endpoint time collars, for which EVERY nonconstant finite-energy strip with $n_z=0$ has onto actual fixed-end Cauchy--Riemann operator. There are finitely many actual index-one strip orbits with $n_z=0$, across all endpoints and Whitney classes, and their modulo-two count matrix satisfies $\widehat\partial^2=0$. These actual chosen counts therefore define a finite chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$.

Every complete pointed splitting can first be made globally weakly admissible by the finite basepoint-avoiding curve isotopies in [[thm-complete-pointed-heegaard-diagrams-admit-globally-weak-admissible-isotopies]]. Consequently a chosen-data complex of this kind can be obtained from every supplied complete splitting of general $Y$. This does not identify complexes before and after those isotopies. It neither imposes global admissibility on ALL inputs of the original sector-specific definition nor proves the construction for every merely sector-admissible diagram. Auxiliary-choice and Heegaard-move invariance, Spin-c decomposition, relative or absolute grading, plus/infinity and cobordism maps remain separate. In genus zero the empty generator gives the one-dimensional complex with zero differential; a possibly empty positive-genus generator set is not asserted to have nonzero homology.

Let $\Sigma$ be a closed Riemann surface, $m\ge1$, and $p\in\Sigma$. In the complex symmetric product $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$ let $E_p=\{p\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}(\Sigma)$. Let $L_0,L_1\subset X$ be compact submanifolds disjoint from $E_p$. Suppose $J_t$ agrees with the fixed complex structure of $X$ on one neighborhood of $E_p$ for every $t\in[0,1]$. Let $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to X$ be a smooth solution of $\partial_\tau u+J_t(u)\partial_tu=0$, with boundary on $L_0,L_1$ and uniform limits as $\tau\to\pm\infty$ at points of $L_0\cap L_1$.

The intersections of $u$ with $E_p$ are a finite collection of interior points, each with positive integral local intersection multiplicity. Their sum is nonnegative, and it is zero exactly when $u$ avoids $E_p$. In pointed Heegaard data, with $L_0,L_1$ the product tori and $p$ any marked point, this proves nonnegativity of the domain multiplicity $n_p(u)$ whenever it is defined by intersection with $E_p$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(\Sigma,j)$ be a closed Riemann surface with positive area form $\eta$, and put $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$, $m\ge1$, with its induced complex structure $J_0$. Let $q:\Sigma^m\to X$ be the quotient, $\Delta\subset X$ its repeated-point locus, and $\Omega=\sum_{l=1}^m\operatorname{pr}_l^*\eta$. Off $\Delta$ the permutation-invariant form $\Omega$ descends to a smooth form $\omega$ on $X\setminus\Delta$. Equip $X$ with any smooth Riemannian metric $g$.

Let $L_\alpha,L_\beta$ be product tori formed from two finite systems of pairwise disjoint attaching curves, with transverse intersections between the systems. Suppose a smooth path $J_t$ agrees with $J_0$ on a neighborhood $V$ of $\Delta$ and tames $\omega$ on $X\setminus V$. Let $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to X$ be a smooth $J_t$-holomorphic strip, with boundary on these tori, finite $g$-Dirichlet energy, and uniform limits at both ends to intersection generators. For each complementary region $R$ of the attaching curves write $n_R(u)$ for the signed intersection multiplicity of $u$ with $\{p\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}(\Sigma)$ at a generic $p\in R$.

There is a constant $C$ depending only on the fixed geometric data and the path, independent of $u$, such that
$$E_g(u)=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R\times[0,1]}(|u_s|_g^2+|u_t|_g^2)\,dsdt\le C\sum_R n_R(u)\int_R\eta.$$
In particular energies of all such representatives with one fixed domain are uniformly bounded. The finite-energy hypothesis here is explicit; no assertion that arbitrary asymptotically convergent smooth solutions automatically have finite energy is included.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix complete singly pointed Heegaard data of any closed oriented three-manifold, a surface complex structure $j$, protected nearly symmetric geometry and exact product generator charts. Let $J_n(s,t)$ converge smoothly with all derivatives to $J_\infty(s,t)$, with uniformly bounded coefficients in one small fixed Cayley neighborhood of that background. Suppose there are autonomous paths $J_n^\pm(t)\to J_\infty^\pm(t)$ such that $J_n(s,t)-J_n^\pm(t)$ tends to zero, with every coefficient derivative, as $s\to\pm\infty$, UNIFORMLY in $n$. This includes families which are exactly autonomous outside one common compact transition interval, and also rapidly decaying source perturbations and their compact-transition truncations. On all protected sets, including every exact generator chart, these structures agree with the common background. At $t=0,1$ their full boundary structures agree with the common background, independently of $s,n$. All source derivatives are uniformly bounded. Let $u_n$ be actual smooth finite-energy solutions of $u_s+J_n(s,t,u)u_t=0$, with the physical product-torus boundaries, generator ends, $n_z(u_n)=0$ and $E(u_n)\le E_0<\infty$.

A subsequence converges to one ANCHORED central strip $u_0$ solving the $J_\infty(s,t)$ equation, possibly constant, together with finitely many ordered nonconstant $J^-_\infty$ strip levels preceding it and finitely many ordered nonconstant $J^+_\infty$ strip levels following it. No nonconstant sphere or boundary-disk bubbles occur. All adjoining generator ends match, the complete energy is the sum of those of these components, and all intervening necks and outer tails lose neither energy nor image diameter. The central map is not divided by translation. Each nonconstant end level is specified up to its ordinary translation. Central convergence and translated end-level convergence are smooth on compact sets, including the physical boundaries.

Eventually the continuous Whitney class of $u_n$ is the concatenation of the ordered end levels, the central class and the remaining end levels. Their actual fixed-end Fredholm indices add to $\operatorname{ind}P_{u_n}$. Here the source-dependent central operator is an actual Fredholm $H^1\to L^2$ operator, with the same kernel/cokernel in its integer higher realizations; its index is the same geometric Whitney index used for the autonomous levels. No regularity, sign of a central index, finite moduli count, gluing collar or chain-map assertion is assumed or concluded.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix compact transverse strip data and a smooth background path $J_t^*$ as in the actual higher Sobolev strip-chart construction, with exact all-$t$ product generator neighborhoods. Assume $J_t^*$ is constant in $t$ on endpoint collars $[0,\eta]$ and $[1-\eta,1]$, where $0<\eta<1/2$. Let $P\subset[0,1]\times X$ be a closed protected set containing those collars and $[0,1]\times V$, where $V$ is an open neighborhood of all generators. The complement $O=([0,1]\times X)\setminus P$ is the free variation region. Spatial neighborhoods of divisors, a diagonal, or any further sets can also be included in $P$. If tameness is required, let $\omega$ be a smooth two-form on an open $W\subset X$, assume the spatial projection of $\overline O$ is a compact subset of $W$, and assume $J_t^*$ is $\omega$-tame on $W$.

There are a separable real Hilbert parameter space $H=\ell^2(\mathbb N;\mathbb R)$, a ball $B_H(0,r)$, and actual smooth paths $J_t(a)$ for $a$ in that ball, such that $J(0)=J^*$, $J(a)^2=-I$, and $J(a)=J^*$ on $P$. In particular every path is constant on the same actual endpoint collars and retains the exact generator charts and all protected values. The family preserves the stated tameness. For every integer $k\ge0$, $a\mapsto J(a)$ is smooth as a map into the global $C^k$ coefficient space, with compatible derivatives at all orders; every $J(a)$ is a smooth path.

At any parameter $a$, finite linear combinations of parameter tangent directions are $C^k$ dense in the smooth compactly supported fields $Y$ on $O$ satisfying $YJ(a)+J(a)Y=0$, for every finite $k$. Their evaluations span that entire anti-complex-linear fiber at each point of $O$. Thus, for each nonzero $v\in T_xX$ and $(t,x)\in O$, the map $b\mapsto(d_aJ[b])_t(x)v$ is onto $T_xX$.

On the actual higher Sobolev strip configuration manifold, this family defines a genuine smooth universal section
$$\mathcal F(a,u)=u_s+J_t(a,u)u_t$$
with the actual local-addition $H^3\cap\mathcal X^1\to H^2$ domain and bundle target. At a zero its derivative is the actual geometric expression
$$d\mathcal F_{(a,u)}(b,\xi)=P_{a,u}\xi+(d_aJ[b])_t(u)u_t,$$
and it has closed range. At any zero where this derivative is onto, the actual universal zero set is locally a separable Hilbert manifold, and its projection to the parameter ball is Fredholm of real index $\operatorname{ind}P_{a,u}$. At such a zero the derivative of that projection is onto if and only if the actual fixed-parameter strip operator $P_{a,u}$ is onto.

This supplies the actual fixed-support parameter family and universal setup. It does not assert that every nonconstant strip has a suitable injective point in $O$, that the universal derivative is onto at every zero, or that a generic parameter has the original global regularity conclusions. In particular interior injective-point density alone does not establish the required availability outside a fixed endpoint collar.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,g)$ be compact and let $L_0,L_1\subset X$ be compact smooth submanifolds whose intersections are finite and transverse. Suppose fixed disjoint coordinate neighborhoods of the intersection points take both submanifolds to linear subspaces, as provided by the product generator charts. Then there is a smooth map
$$\mathcal E:\{(x,v)\in TX:|v|_g<\epsilon\}\longrightarrow X$$
for some $\epsilon>0$, with $\mathcal E(x,0)=x$, $d_v\mathcal E(x,0)=I$, and $\mathcal E(x,v)\in L_j$ whenever $x\in L_j$, $v\in T_xL_j$. The map $(x,v)\mapsto(x,\mathcal E(x,v))$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open neighborhood of the diagonal in $X\times X$ after shrinking its domain. Its inverse for sufficiently close pairs in $L_j\times L_j$ takes values in $TL_j$.

On smaller fixed generator neighborhoods it is exactly coordinate addition:
$$q(\mathcal E(x,v))=q(x)+dq_xv$$
for all sufficiently small $v$. Derivatives of every fixed order of this addition and its inverse are uniformly bounded on smaller neighborhoods in finite coordinate covers. This is a genuine finite-dimensional boundary-preserving local addition, not an assumption about a Sobolev map space.

Assume Countable Choice and put $S=\mathbb R\times(0,1)$. For $k=1,2,3$ there is a bounded linear extension $H^k(S)\to H^k(\mathbb R^2)$, using no boundary condition. The spaces have the estimates $H^1(S)\subset L^4(S)$, $H^2(S)\subset C^0(\overline S)\cap L^\infty(S)$, and $H^3(S)\subset C^1(\overline S)$, with bounded supremum norms in the last two assertions. In particular
$$\|fg\|_{H^2}\le C\|f\|_{H^2}\|g\|_{H^2}.$$

Fix smooth $\rho\ge0$ equal to $|s|$ outside a compact interval, with bounded derivatives, and $\delta\ge0$. Set $w=e^{\delta\rho}$ and $\|u\|_{H^k_\delta}=\|wu\|_{H^k}$. The same embeddings hold with $w|u|$, or $w(|u|+|du|)$ for $k=3$, bounded by the weighted norm. Products satisfy
$$\|fg\|_{H^2_\delta}\le C_\delta\|f\|_{H^2_\delta}\|g\|_{H^2_\delta},\qquad \|du\|_{H^2_\delta}\le C_\delta\|u\|_{H^3_\delta}.$$

Let $h(s,t,z)$ be smooth up to the boundary for $z$ in a finite-dimensional ball about zero, with bounded mixed derivatives of source order at most two and every finite target order on smaller target balls, and $h(s,t,0)=0$. Then $u\mapsto h(s,t,u)$ is a smooth map from the open subset of $H^2_\delta$ whose supremum lies in that ball to $H^2_\delta$. Its derivatives are the ordinary pointwise derivatives of $h$. On a sufficiently small bounded norm ball the remainder $Q(u)=h(s,t,u)-h_z(s,t,0)u$ satisfies
$$\|Q(u)-Q(v)\|_{H^2_\delta}\le C\bigl(\|u\|_{H^2_\delta}+\|v\|_{H^2_\delta}\bigr)\|u-v\|_{H^2_\delta}.$$
All statements hold componentwise for finite-dimensional real or complex targets.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix compact $(X,g)$, compact transverse boundary submanifolds $L_0,L_1$, and a smooth $J_t$ with fixed totally real boundary structures. Suppose fixed disjoint generator charts about their finite intersection identify the boundaries with $\mathbb R^m,i\mathbb R^m$ and $J_t$ with $i$ for every $t$. Fix end generators $x_-,x_+$ and $0\le\delta<\pi/2$, using a smooth weight $e^{\delta\rho(s)}$ as in the weighted Sobolev algebra lemma.

There is an actual second-countable separable real Hilbert configuration manifold $\mathcal B_\delta$ of strip maps with these boundary values and ends, constructed as the union of the following local charts. A reference map $u_0$ is smooth, satisfies the boundary condition, and equals $x_\pm$ outside a compact longitudinal interval. Its tangent model is
$$\mathcal X_{u_0}=H^3_\delta(u_0^*TX)\cap\mathcal X^1_{u_0},$$
where $\mathcal X^1_{u_0}$ is the $H^1$ completion of compactly supported smooth tangent sections satisfying $TL_0,TL_1$ on the edges. This is an intersection with the $H^1$ domain, not an asserted $H^3$ closure. Small sections give maps $u=\mathcal E(u_0,\xi)$ for the actual boundary-preserving local addition. All smooth finite-energy $J_t$ strips with these ends belong to this manifold.

The actual Cauchy–Riemann expression $u_s+J_t(u)u_t$ defines a smooth section of the Hilbert bundle with fiber $H^2_\delta(u^*TX)$. In the local-addition trivialization it is a smooth map $\mathcal F_{u_0}:\mathcal X_{u_0}\to H^2_\delta(u_0^*TX)$. On a small norm ball its nonlinear remainder obeys
$$\|\mathcal F(\xi)-\mathcal F(\eta)-D\mathcal F(0)(\xi-\eta)\|_{H^2_\delta}\le C(\|\xi\|_{H^3_\delta}+\|\eta\|_{H^3_\delta})\|\xi-\eta\|_{H^3_\delta}.$$
The constants are uniform for reference families with uniform coefficient/frame derivatives through the orders used in this estimate. Every zero is smooth and has finite energy and the prescribed ends. At each zero the derivative is the actual geometric Fredholm linearization $H^3_\delta\cap\mathcal X^1\to H^2_\delta$, with the same real index as its $H^1\to L^2$ realization, before translation quotient. No universal transversality or gluing is claimed.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $u$ be an actual smooth finite-energy strip in the compact exact-generator geometry of the actual higher Sobolev strip-chart construction, and let $P:H^1\cap\mathcal X^1\to L^2$ be its geometric Cauchy–Riemann linearization. Use any fixed smooth positive definite target metric and source measure $ds\,dt$ to define the real $L^2$ pairing. Every $\eta\in L^2$ which annihilates $\operatorname{Ran}P$ has a smooth representative on $\mathbb R\times(0,1)$. In each smooth local frame that representative satisfies the actual formal adjoint equation. For compact subsets $K\subset\operatorname{int}U$ in a coordinate patch inside the strip and every integer $q\ge0$,
$$\|\eta\|_{H^q(K)}\le C_{K,U,q}\|\eta\|_{L^2(U)},$$
where the constant depends on the indicated compact containment and finitely many local smooth coefficient and metric bounds. No boundary regularity or adjoint boundary formula is asserted.

More generally, let $K_0:H\to H^2(u^*TX)$ be any bounded linear parameter derivative from a real Hilbert space, including the actual derivative $b\mapsto(d_aJ[b])_t(u)u_t$ of the smooth Hilbert family. The operators
$$A_0(\xi,b)=P\xi+K_0b:\ (H^1\cap\mathcal X^1)\oplus H\longrightarrow L^2,$$
$$A_2(\xi,b)=P\xi+K_0b:\ (H^3\cap\mathcal X^1)\oplus H\longrightarrow H^2$$
both have closed range, and $A_0$ is onto if and only if $A_2$ is onto. They are onto exactly when there is no nonzero $L^2$ section $\eta$ such that
$$\langle\eta,P\xi\rangle_{L^2}=0\quad\hbox{for every }\xi\in H^1\cap\mathcal X^1,\qquad \langle\eta,K_0b\rangle_{L^2}=0\quad\hbox{for every }b\in H.$$
Each such obstruction is smooth on the interior by the first assertion. Thus actual interior unique continuation can be applied to an $L^2$ obstruction after this lemma; an $H^2$-dual distribution need not be mistaken for an $L^2$ function. The lemma does not prove unique continuation or rule out the displayed obstructions.

Assume countable choice and write $D=\partial_s+i\partial_t=2\partial_{\bar z}$ on a connected open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb C$. Let $B\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb R}(\mathbb C^m))$, and let $v\in W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb C^m)$, for some $p>2$, solve $Dv+Bv=0$ weakly. Use its continuous representative. Near every point $z_0$ there are a continuous invertible complex matrix $P$, belonging locally to $W^{1,q}$ for every finite $q>2$, and a holomorphic vector function $h$ with $v=Ph$. One may normalize $P(z_0)=I$.

Consequently either $v$ is identically zero, or all its zeros are isolated and have finite order: at a zero $z_0$ there are an integer $k\ge1$ and constants $c,C,r>0$ with
$$c|z-z_0|^k\le|v(z)|\le C|z-z_0|^k\qquad(0<|z-z_0|<r).$$
In particular vanishing on an open set, or vanishing to infinite order at one point, forces global vanishing. The same conclusions hold for $v_s+J(s,t)v_t+Av=0$ when $J$ is a smooth family of real complex structures and $A$ is locally bounded; the local factor is then an invertible real matrix rather than necessarily a complex matrix.

If two smooth maps solve the same equation $u_s+J(s,t,u)u_t=0$ for a smooth almost complex family on a smooth target and have matching infinite jets at one interior point, they agree everywhere on their connected common source. Agreement on an open set suffices. This assertion concerns parametrized maps and actual linear equations; it does not infer moduli transversality or an injective-point theorem.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix $m\ge1$ and angles $0<\theta_j<\pi$ for $1\le j\le m$. On the strip $S=\mathbb R\times[0,1]$ impose the real product-plane boundary conditions $u(s,0)\in\mathbb R^m$ and $u(s,1)\in\prod_j e^{i\theta_j}\mathbb R$. Let $H^1_\theta$ be the completion of smooth maps satisfying these conditions and compactly supported in the $s$ direction, for the norm
$$\|u\|_{H^1}^2=\|u\|_2^2+\|u_s\|_2^2+\|u_t\|_2^2.$$
The real linear operator $D=\partial_s+i\partial_t$ extends to an isomorphism $H^1_\theta\to L^2(S;\mathbb C^m)$. Put $\gamma=\min_j\{\theta_j,\pi-\theta_j\}>0$. Its inverse satisfies
$$\|D^{-1}f\|_2\le\gamma^{-1}\|f\|_2,\qquad \|D^{-1}f\|_{H^1}\le\sqrt{\gamma^{-2}+5}\,\|f\|_2.$$
For $0\le\delta<\gamma$, set $w(s)=e^{\delta|s|}$, $H^1_{\theta,\delta}=\{u:wu\in H^1_\theta\}$ with norm $\|wu\|_{H^1}$, and $L^2_\delta=\{f:wf\in L^2\}$ with norm $\|wf\|_2$. Then $D:H^1_{\theta,\delta}\to L^2_\delta$ is an isomorphism and
$$\|D^{-1}f\|_{H^1_{\theta,\delta}}\le\frac{\sqrt{\gamma^{-2}+5}}{1-\delta/\gamma}\,\|f\|_{L^2_\delta},\qquad \|wD^{-1}f\|_2\le\frac{\|wf\|_2}{\gamma-\delta}.$$
These are estimates for the constant linear asymptotic model. They make no assertion about nonlinear strip decay, a variable-coefficient operator, or its Maslov index.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $S=\mathbb R_s\times[0,1]_t$, $m\ge1$, and $0<\theta_j<\pi$. Write $X_0=H^1_\theta$ for the real $H^1$ completion of smooth maps compactly supported in $s$ satisfying $u(s,0)\in\mathbb R^m$ and $u(s,1)\in\prod_j e^{i\theta_j}\mathbb R$. Let $B:S\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb R}(\mathbb C^m)$ be smooth up to the boundary, with every derivative bounded, and suppose its uniform end limits are real diagonal matrices $\operatorname{diag}(b_{\pm,j})$ with $\theta_j-b_{\pm,j}\notin\pi\mathbb Z$. For an integer $q\ge0$ put
$$X_q=H^{q+1}(S;\mathbb C^m)\cap X_0,\qquad Y_q=H^q(S;\mathbb C^m),\qquad T_q=\partial_s+i\partial_t+B:X_q\longrightarrow Y_q,$$
using real Hilbert spaces and their indicated Sobolev norms. There are no higher boundary conditions: only the zeroth trace encoded by $X_0$ is required. In particular no normal derivative or forcing trace is prescribed.

Every $T_q$ is bounded Fredholm. Its kernel is the same set as the kernel of $T_0$, and its range is $Y_q\cap\operatorname{Ran}T_0$. The inclusion of $Y_q$ in $L^2$ induces an isomorphism of real cokernels. Thus
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}T_q=\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}T_0=\sum_j\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\theta_j-b_{-,j}}\pi\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\frac{\theta_j-b_{+,j}}\pi\right\rfloor\right).$$
More precisely, if $u\in X_0$ and $T_0u=f\in H^q$, then $u\in X_q$ and
$$\|u\|_{H^{q+1}}\le C_q\bigl(\|f\|_{H^q}+\|u\|_{H^1}\bigr).$$

The same conclusions hold with smooth two-sided weights $w=e^{\delta\rho(s)}$, where $\rho$ is smooth, equals $|s|$ outside a compact interval, has all derivatives of positive order bounded, and $0\le\delta<\min_{\pm,j,n}|\pi n-\theta_j+b_{\pm,j}|$. Weighted spaces mean $wu\in X_q$ and $wf\in Y_q$. Their index is the same displayed index. The weight is smooth at zero even for $q\ge1$.

Finally, for an actual geometric strip operator with exact product-integrable ends and the smooth bundle frame supplied by the geometric strip normal-form theorem, the actual $H^{q+1}$ boundary-section domain and $H^q$ target have this same real index before translation quotient, also with these smooth weights. This asserts integer Hilbert Sobolev agreement; no $W^{1,p}$ comparison or Heegaard-domain Euler formula is asserted.

Assume countable choice. Let $E,Y$ be real Banach spaces, $f$ a $C^1$ map on an open neighborhood of the closed ball $\overline B_E(0,r)$, and $D=df(0)$. Suppose a specified bounded linear map $Q:Y\to E$ satisfies $DQ=I_Y$. Fix $M>0$, $L\ge0$ with $\|Q\|\le M$ and
$$\|df(x)-df(y)\|\le L\|x-y\|\quad(x,y\in\overline B_E(0,r)).$$
Put $\varepsilon=\|f(0)\|$. If
$$2M\varepsilon<r,\qquad MLr\le\tfrac12,$$
then there is a unique $x\in\operatorname{im}Q\cap\overline B_E(0,r)$ with $f(x)=0$. It satisfies
$$\|x\|\le2M\varepsilon,\qquad \|x+Qf(0)\|\le2M^3L\varepsilon^2.$$
The sequence $x_0=0$,
$$x_{n+1}=-Qf(0)-Q\bigl(f(x_n)-f(0)-Dx_n\bigr)$$
converges to this correction, with contraction ratio at most $1/2$. At the corrected zero $df(x)$ is still surjective, with specified right inverse
$$Q_x=Q\bigl[I_Y+(df(x)-D)Q\bigr]^{-1},\qquad \|Q_x\|\le2M.$$

The following local smooth conclusions also hold. If $f(0)=0$, $f$ is $C^q$, $1\le q\le\infty$, and $D$ has the specified bounded right inverse $Q$, continuity of $df$ alone suffices for a local $C^q$ zero-set chart. With $K=\ker D$ and $V=\operatorname{im}Q$, there is a $C^q$ map $v$ from a neighborhood of $0$ in $K$ to $V$, with $v(0)=dv(0)=0$, such that, in a product neighborhood for $E=K\oplus V$,
$$f(k+w)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad w=v(k).$$
For a $C^q$ family $f(p,z)$, $p$ in any Banach parameter space, the same assertion holds locally with $v=v(p,k)$ whenever $f(p_0,0)=0$ and $d_zf(p_0,0)Q=I_Y$. In particular, if $Q(p)$ is a specified $C^q$ family of right inverses to $d_zf(p,0)$ and the quantitative hypotheses hold strictly with locally uniform constants, the unique corrections in $\operatorname{im}Q(p)$ depend $C^q$ on $p$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $E$ be a smooth real rank-$2m$ vector bundle on $S=\mathbb R_s\times[0,1]_t$, $m\ge1$, with a smooth endomorphism $J$ satisfying $J^2=-I$. On the two boundary edges let $F_0,F_1$ be smooth real rank-$m$ subbundles with $F_j\cap JF_j=0$. Suppose that outside a compact strip there are specified smooth complex frames $\tau_\pm:\mathbb C^m\to E$, intertwining $i$ and $J$, in which $F_0=\mathbb R^m$ and $F_1=i\mathbb R^m$. Let $P$ be a smooth real linear first-order operator on sections of $E$ with symbol
$$P(f\xi)=fP\xi+f_s\xi+f_tJ\xi$$
for every smooth real function $f$, and suppose its expression in each end frame is exactly $\partial_s+i\partial_t$ outside a compact strip.

There exist a global smooth complex frame $\Phi$, a sign matrix $S_+=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma,1,\ldots,1)$ with $\sigma\in\{1,-1\}$, an integer $\ell$, and a smooth real function $\vartheta(s)$, constant at $\pi/2$ on the negative end and $\pi/2+\ell\pi$ on the positive end, such that $\Phi=\tau_-$ on the negative end, $\Phi=\tau_+S_+$ on the positive end, and
$$F_0=\Phi\mathbb R^m,\qquad F_1=\Phi\left(e^{i\vartheta(s)}\mathbb R\times i\mathbb R^{m-1}\right).$$
In this frame $P$ is $\partial_s+i\partial_t+B(s,t)$ with smooth compactly supported real linear $B$. On the $H^1$ completion of compactly supported smooth sections satisfying those actual boundary subbundles, with the norm defined by finite bundle charts on a compact core and the prescribed frames on the ends, $P$ maps to the corresponding $L^2(E)$ space and is real Fredholm, with
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}P=-\ell.$$
The same index holds with the weight $e^{\delta|s|}$ for $0\le\delta<\pi/2$. These are indices before any translation quotient. The integer $\ell$ is independent of the choices in the construction, since it is minus the index of this fixed operator.

In particular the conclusion applies to the actual linearization at a smooth $J_t$-holomorphic strip of finite Dirichlet energy, measured in a smooth target metric, in a compact target, with compact totally real boundary submanifolds of transverse finite intersection, whenever the chosen target charts at their intersections identify those submanifolds with $\mathbb R^m,i\mathbb R^m$ and $J_t$ with the constant structure $i$ for every $t$. For product Heegaard tori such a geometric choice is available by the product-integrable generator-neighborhood construction. No domain Euler-measure formula, corner/excision theorem, generic regularity, or moduli count is part of this conclusion.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix complete singly pointed Heegaard data of any closed oriented three-manifold, a surface complex structure $j$, protected nearly symmetric geometry and exact product generator charts. Let $J_n(s,t)$ converge smoothly with all derivatives to $J_\infty(s,t)$, with uniformly bounded coefficients in one small fixed Cayley neighborhood of that background. Suppose there are autonomous paths $J_n^\pm(t)\to J_\infty^\pm(t)$ such that $J_n(s,t)-J_n^\pm(t)$ tends to zero, with every coefficient derivative, as $s\to\pm\infty$, UNIFORMLY in $n$. This includes families which are exactly autonomous outside one common compact transition interval, and also rapidly decaying source perturbations and their compact-transition truncations. On all protected sets, including every exact generator chart, these structures agree with the common background. At $t=0,1$ their full boundary structures agree with the common background, independently of $s,n$. All source derivatives are uniformly bounded. Let $u_n$ be actual smooth finite-energy solutions of $u_s+J_n(s,t,u)u_t=0$, with the physical product-torus boundaries, generator ends, $n_z(u_n)=0$ and $E(u_n)\le E_0<\infty$.

A subsequence converges to one ANCHORED central strip $u_0$ solving the $J_\infty(s,t)$ equation, possibly constant, together with finitely many ordered nonconstant $J^-_\infty$ strip levels preceding it and finitely many ordered nonconstant $J^+_\infty$ strip levels following it. No nonconstant sphere or boundary-disk bubbles occur. All adjoining generator ends match, the complete energy is the sum of those of these components, and all intervening necks and outer tails lose neither energy nor image diameter. The central map is not divided by translation. Each nonconstant end level is specified up to its ordinary translation. Central convergence and translated end-level convergence are smooth on compact sets, including the physical boundaries.

Eventually the continuous Whitney class of $u_n$ is the concatenation of the ordered end levels, the central class and the remaining end levels. Their actual fixed-end Fredholm indices add to $\operatorname{ind}P_{u_n}$. Here the source-dependent central operator is an actual Fredholm $H^1\to L^2$ operator, with the same kernel/cokernel in its integer higher realizations; its index is the same geometric Whitney index used for the autonomous levels. No regularity, sign of a central index, finite moduli count, gluing collar or chain-map assertion is assumed or concluded.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix a globally weakly admissible complete singly pointed diagram of ANY closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold, with one surface complex structure $j$, area form and protected nearly symmetric geometry. Use a small Cayley coefficient ball about the standard background, with common exact product generator charts. Let $J^-_t,J^+_t$ be two paths in that ball, constant on genuine endpoint time collars with the same endpoint values as the background. Suppose EVERY nonconstant zero-basepoint strip for either path is regular, in the actual fixed-end $H^1\to L^2$ realization. There is a smooth source-dependent path $K(s,t)$ in the same protected coefficient neighborhood, equal to $J^-_t$ for all sufficiently negative $s$ and to $J^+_t$ for all sufficiently positive $s$, constant on genuine positive time collars at $t=0,1$, with the following properties. EVERY actual nonconstant finite-energy solution with uniform generator ends of
$$u_s+K(s,t,u)u_t=0,\qquad u(s,0)\in T_\alpha,\quad u(s,1)\in T_\beta,\qquad n_z(u)=0$$
has onto actual fixed-end operator, in every integer higher realization. Its constant solutions are the generator maps and have invertible index-zero operators. Across all endpoints and realized classes there are finitely many actual index-zero solutions. They are counted WITHOUT a translation quotient: the source transition is fixed. Thus their mod-two numbers define a finite matrix from the $J^-$ generator module to the $J^+$ generator module.

More generally, ANY fixed compact-transition structure in this same family, with these end paths and regular at EVERY zero-basepoint solution, has a finite actual index-zero solution set, by the same anchored argument. The construction proves that such choices exist.

This is regularity and finite continuation counts, not yet a chain-map, composition or chain-equivalence theorem. It compares only the specified common integrable background and protected small family. Changing $j$, comparing merely sector-admissible inputs, Heegaard moves, gradings and plus/infinity maps remain separate. Genus zero gives only the point solution and its identity one-by-one count matrix.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,g)$ be compact and let $L_0,L_1\subset X$ be compact smooth submanifolds whose intersections are finite and transverse. Suppose fixed disjoint coordinate neighborhoods of the intersection points take both submanifolds to linear subspaces, as provided by the product generator charts. Then there is a smooth map
$$\mathcal E:\{(x,v)\in TX:|v|_g<\epsilon\}\longrightarrow X$$
for some $\epsilon>0$, with $\mathcal E(x,0)=x$, $d_v\mathcal E(x,0)=I$, and $\mathcal E(x,v)\in L_j$ whenever $x\in L_j$, $v\in T_xL_j$. The map $(x,v)\mapsto(x,\mathcal E(x,v))$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open neighborhood of the diagonal in $X\times X$ after shrinking its domain. Its inverse for sufficiently close pairs in $L_j\times L_j$ takes values in $TL_j$.

On smaller fixed generator neighborhoods it is exactly coordinate addition:
$$q(\mathcal E(x,v))=q(x)+dq_xv$$
for all sufficiently small $v$. Derivatives of every fixed order of this addition and its inverse are uniformly bounded on smaller neighborhoods in finite coordinate covers. This is a genuine finite-dimensional boundary-preserving local addition, not an assumption about a Sobolev map space.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix compact $(X,g)$, compact transverse boundary submanifolds $L_0,L_1$, and a smooth $J_t$ with fixed totally real boundary structures. Suppose fixed disjoint generator charts about their finite intersection identify the boundaries with $\mathbb R^m,i\mathbb R^m$ and $J_t$ with $i$ for every $t$. Fix end generators $x_-,x_+$ and $0\le\delta<\pi/2$, using a smooth weight $e^{\delta\rho(s)}$ as in the weighted Sobolev algebra lemma.

There is an actual second-countable separable real Hilbert configuration manifold $\mathcal B_\delta$ of strip maps with these boundary values and ends, constructed as the union of the following local charts. A reference map $u_0$ is smooth, satisfies the boundary condition, and equals $x_\pm$ outside a compact longitudinal interval. Its tangent model is
$$\mathcal X_{u_0}=H^3_\delta(u_0^*TX)\cap\mathcal X^1_{u_0},$$
where $\mathcal X^1_{u_0}$ is the $H^1$ completion of compactly supported smooth tangent sections satisfying $TL_0,TL_1$ on the edges. This is an intersection with the $H^1$ domain, not an asserted $H^3$ closure. Small sections give maps $u=\mathcal E(u_0,\xi)$ for the actual boundary-preserving local addition. All smooth finite-energy $J_t$ strips with these ends belong to this manifold.

The actual Cauchy–Riemann expression $u_s+J_t(u)u_t$ defines a smooth section of the Hilbert bundle with fiber $H^2_\delta(u^*TX)$. In the local-addition trivialization it is a smooth map $\mathcal F_{u_0}:\mathcal X_{u_0}\to H^2_\delta(u_0^*TX)$. On a small norm ball its nonlinear remainder obeys
$$\|\mathcal F(\xi)-\mathcal F(\eta)-D\mathcal F(0)(\xi-\eta)\|_{H^2_\delta}\le C(\|\xi\|_{H^3_\delta}+\|\eta\|_{H^3_\delta})\|\xi-\eta\|_{H^3_\delta}.$$
The constants are uniform for reference families with uniform coefficient/frame derivatives through the orders used in this estimate. Every zero is smooth and has finite energy and the prescribed ends. At each zero the derivative is the actual geometric Fredholm linearization $H^3_\delta\cap\mathcal X^1\to H^2_\delta$, with the same real index as its $H^1\to L^2$ realization, before translation quotient. No universal transversality or gluing is claimed.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $S=\mathbb R_s\times[0,1]_t$, $m\ge1$, and $0<\theta_j<\pi$. Write $X_0=H^1_\theta$ for the real $H^1$ completion of smooth maps compactly supported in $s$ satisfying $u(s,0)\in\mathbb R^m$ and $u(s,1)\in\prod_j e^{i\theta_j}\mathbb R$. Let $B:S\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb R}(\mathbb C^m)$ be smooth up to the boundary, with every derivative bounded, and suppose its uniform end limits are real diagonal matrices $\operatorname{diag}(b_{\pm,j})$ with $\theta_j-b_{\pm,j}\notin\pi\mathbb Z$. For an integer $q\ge0$ put
$$X_q=H^{q+1}(S;\mathbb C^m)\cap X_0,\qquad Y_q=H^q(S;\mathbb C^m),\qquad T_q=\partial_s+i\partial_t+B:X_q\longrightarrow Y_q,$$
using real Hilbert spaces and their indicated Sobolev norms. There are no higher boundary conditions: only the zeroth trace encoded by $X_0$ is required. In particular no normal derivative or forcing trace is prescribed.

Every $T_q$ is bounded Fredholm. Its kernel is the same set as the kernel of $T_0$, and its range is $Y_q\cap\operatorname{Ran}T_0$. The inclusion of $Y_q$ in $L^2$ induces an isomorphism of real cokernels. Thus
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}T_q=\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}T_0=\sum_j\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\theta_j-b_{-,j}}\pi\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\frac{\theta_j-b_{+,j}}\pi\right\rfloor\right).$$
More precisely, if $u\in X_0$ and $T_0u=f\in H^q$, then $u\in X_q$ and
$$\|u\|_{H^{q+1}}\le C_q\bigl(\|f\|_{H^q}+\|u\|_{H^1}\bigr).$$

The same conclusions hold with smooth two-sided weights $w=e^{\delta\rho(s)}$, where $\rho$ is smooth, equals $|s|$ outside a compact interval, has all derivatives of positive order bounded, and $0\le\delta<\min_{\pm,j,n}|\pi n-\theta_j+b_{\pm,j}|$. Weighted spaces mean $wu\in X_q$ and $wf\in Y_q$. Their index is the same displayed index. The weight is smooth at zero even for $q\ge1$.

Finally, for an actual geometric strip operator with exact product-integrable ends and the smooth bundle frame supplied by the geometric strip normal-form theorem, the actual $H^{q+1}$ boundary-section domain and $H^q$ target have this same real index before translation quotient, also with these smooth weights. This asserts integer Hilbert Sobolev agreement; no $W^{1,p}$ comparison or Heegaard-domain Euler formula is asserted.

Assume countable choice. Let $E,Y$ be real Banach spaces, $f$ a $C^1$ map on an open neighborhood of the closed ball $\overline B_E(0,r)$, and $D=df(0)$. Suppose a specified bounded linear map $Q:Y\to E$ satisfies $DQ=I_Y$. Fix $M>0$, $L\ge0$ with $\|Q\|\le M$ and
$$\|df(x)-df(y)\|\le L\|x-y\|\quad(x,y\in\overline B_E(0,r)).$$
Put $\varepsilon=\|f(0)\|$. If
$$2M\varepsilon<r,\qquad MLr\le\tfrac12,$$
then there is a unique $x\in\operatorname{im}Q\cap\overline B_E(0,r)$ with $f(x)=0$. It satisfies
$$\|x\|\le2M\varepsilon,\qquad \|x+Qf(0)\|\le2M^3L\varepsilon^2.$$
The sequence $x_0=0$,
$$x_{n+1}=-Qf(0)-Q\bigl(f(x_n)-f(0)-Dx_n\bigr)$$
converges to this correction, with contraction ratio at most $1/2$. At the corrected zero $df(x)$ is still surjective, with specified right inverse
$$Q_x=Q\bigl[I_Y+(df(x)-D)Q\bigr]^{-1},\qquad \|Q_x\|\le2M.$$

Put $\varepsilon=\|f(0)\|$. If
$$2M\varepsilon<r,\qquad MLr\le\tfrac12,$$
then there is a unique $x\in\operatorname{im}Q\cap\overline B_E(0,r)$ with $f(x)=0$. It satisfies
